events.text: The Jade Furnace House keeps its sealed jar in the third treasury, under a lacquer lid painted with a sleeping centipede. You lift it in the hour before dawn. Inside, a dozen worms the colour of fingernails turn toward your warmth.

effects.log: You take one in a silver box and are back in your bed before the drum.

choices.text: Leave a coin for the furnace-keeper

effects.log: You leave a coin. Ma Ilsun will know someone was here, and that they were polite.

events.text: Furnace-Keeper Ma Ilsun is awake, sitting on a stool beside the jar with a lamp turned low. "Of the blood," she says, "and a thief. The house will hear of both."

effects.log: She will not keep it, but she tells it kindly.
You run. The lamp falls and burns your hand on the way out.

events.text: The keeper of the Cult's treasury opens a door nobody has opened in your reign. Inside is a jar sealed with the mark of a Heavenly Demon dead four hundred years, and something inside it moves.

effects.log: Two worms, very old, very still. They know whose hand this is.

choices.text: Ask what it was used for

effects.log: The keeper tells you. You wish you had not asked, and keep the jar anyway.

events.text: Elder Ahn Seolhwa of your sect gives you a jar the size of a fist and will not say what is in it until you are alone. "A heart-binding gu," she says then. "For the day you need someone to be loyal. Pray that day never comes."

effects.log: She pats your hand. Her fingers are cold.

choices.text: Ask if she has used one

effects.log: She looks at you for a long time and says, "Twice."

events.text: In a rotting log in the southern forest you find a nest of worms that should not exist: they turn toward your blood, and the poison in your body does not frighten them. A heart-binding gu, wild.

effects.log: You take the largest one in a bamboo tube.

choices.text: Take it, and burn the nest

effects.log: You take one and burn the rest. One is enough for anyone.

events.text: You feed the jar on centipedes, rice wine and patience all summer. The worms grow fat and quiet, and when you lift the lid they turn toward you all together.

effects.log: You count them twice. It is a strange thing to be proud of.
You put the lid back. Your hand is shaking a little.

events.text: A hot summer. When you lift the lid there are fewer worms than there were, and the ones left are fat and very still.

effects.log: You feed them more. They are always hungry.

choices.text: Move the jar to the cellar

effects.log: Cool earth and dark. The fat ones stir again by autumn, and fewer die the next summer.

events.text: You open a vein over the jar at midnight and let it drink. The worms turn the colour of your blood and lie down together like puppies.

effects.log: You bind the wound with clean cloth and sit very still until the dizziness passes.
You watch until they are done. It takes longer than you thought.

events.text: The second time the jar drinks more, and you are dizzy for a week. When you hold the jar now you can feel the worms in it the way you feel your own fingers.

effects.log: You bind the wound with clean cloth and sit very still until the dizziness passes.
You watch until they are done. It takes longer than you thought.

events.text: The third fusion. The worms are blood of your blood now. When you think of anyone the worms hold, you feel their heartbeat beside your own.

effects.log: You bind the wound with clean cloth and sit very still until the dizziness passes.
You watch until they are done. It takes longer than you thought.

events.text: Your people catch {hgu_name} in the rafters above your rooms with a notebook full of your comings and goings. They will not say who sent them.

effects.log: You hand them over.

choices.text: Keep them in a locked room for now

effects.log: You keep them. You have a jar that could make them useful.

choices.text: Let them go with a warning

effects.log: You let them go. They run, and do not look back.

events.text: {hgu_name}, a servant who has been with your house a year, is found reading your letters by candlelight. The seal on the last one was broken very neatly.

effects.log: You hand them over.
You lock the door and think about the jar.

events.text: {hgu_name}, a retainer of {hgu_master}, sits across a low table from you in a back room of a wine shop. They have been told you want to buy information. They do not yet know what you want to buy.

effects.log: You pour. They drink. The worm is in your sleeve still, waiting for a second cup.
You talk. They are clever, and unhappy with their master, and you file both away.

events.text: {hgu_name} kneels for what they think is a blessing. You lay your hand on their chest and the worm goes in, quick as a thought. They gasp, once, and look up at you with eyes that understand.

effects.log: You tell them. They do not cry. That is worse.
You tell them nothing. They will learn what it is the day they think of leaving.

events.text: {hgu_name} swallows the second cup with the worm in it. You tell them what it was. From tonight they spy for you, and against whoever sent them.

effects.log: You give it. They obey with their whole face shut.

choices.text: Give them a little silver too

effects.log: You give them silver. A worm and a wage: it is almost a job.

events.text: {hgu_name} wakes on the floor of the back room with a sore chest and a new master. {hgu_master} will hear nothing you do not want heard.

effects.log: You explain the worm, calmly. They are sick on the floor.

choices.text: Offer them a way out one day

effects.log: You promise to call the worm back when this is over. They do not believe you.

events.text: {hgu_name} tried to move against you. The worm turned in their heart, and they lay on the floor until dawn with their hands over their chest. In the morning they come to you grey-faced and kneel.

effects.log: You keep them. They will not try again soon.

choices.text: Call the worm out of them

effects.log: Enough. You call the worm back.
You let the worm finish what it started.

events.text: {hgu_name} went to your enemies with what they know, and got as far as the door. The worm turned. Now they lie in your courtyard where they fell, alive, waiting to hear what you will do.

effects.log: You pick them up and carry them inside. They will not forget it, either way.

choices.text: Call the worm out of them

effects.log: You call it back. Let them go to whoever they like.
You let the worm finish what it started.

events.text: {hgu_name} burned the worm out of their own heart with a hot needle and a pint of strong spirit, and walked out of your life cursing your name in every teahouse on the road.

effects.log: You let them go. The secret goes with them.

choices.text: Count what is left in the jar

effects.log: You count the worms left. You will need to be more careful.

events.text: You hum the note that calls it, and the worm comes up out of {hgu_name}'s heart and into your palm. {hgu_name} looks at it for a long time, then at you.

effects.log: You say it. They nod, once. It is more than you deserve.
You say nothing. They leave without a word.

events.text: The murim knows. In every teahouse they say you keep worms in jars and put them in the hearts of people who trusted you. Righteous sects send back your letters unopened.

effects.log: "Loyalty is precious," you say. "I make sure of it." Some people find that admirable. Not many.
You deny it to anyone who will listen.
You say the Cult did it to you. Some people believe that.

events.text: {hgu_name} brings you tea every morning now, and never meets your eyes. Sometimes, when they think you are not looking, they put a hand over their heart.

effects.log: You thank them. Their hand trembles on the cup.
They say they sleep well. They are lying, and you both know it.

events.text: {hgu_name} slips you a folded note at the market: names, a date, a place. Someone was planning something. Now they are not.

effects.log: You burn it. You remember every word.
{hgu_name} only looks at you. You do not ask again, and you sleep a little worse.

events.text: {hgu_name} comes back from {hgu_master}'s house with news, as always. Today they also ask, very quietly, how long.

effects.log: You do not know. You say so. It is the only honest thing you have said to them.

choices.text: Tell them it will not be long

effects.log: You lie. They nod, and go back.
